translation_notes: Driver cannot execute the region: original.py fails at 'from pyontutils.namespaces import PREFIXES as uPREFIXES' (ModuleNotFoundError: pyontutils is not installed), and even past that main() calls docopt(__doc__, ...) against sys.argv and reads six hardcoded '{prefix}/NIF-Ontology/ttl/generated/*.ttl' paths from disk, then writes four '*.conf' files as a side effect -- external package, CLI parsing, filesystem and network-fetched-ontology dependencies with no injectable single graph. translation_status stays draft, classification excluded (see AGENT_BATCH.md order-of-priority point 1); fixture.ttl left as the unfilled placeholder since there is no single-graph entry point to feed it.

Independently of the execution problem, the ns_def_local site itself (line ~24, 'ilxtr = rdflib.Namespace(uPREFIXES["ilxtr"])') is NOT EXPRESSIBLE as '@prefix': confirmed by transpiling a minimal repro ('@prefix ilxtr: <{PREFIXES["ilxtr"]}> .') -- the transpiler rejects an interpolated/dynamic IRI in a @prefix declaration with a plain SyntaxError. '@prefix' only accepts a literal <IRI> (or an f-string only inside f<...>/e<...> term forms, not inside the declaration itself). Here the namespace IRI is a runtime dict lookup (uPREFIXES['ilxtr'], populated from pyontutils.namespaces at import time), not a literal known at transpile time, so this instance of the ns_def_local idiom has no ldpy construction to move to -- kept as plain rdflib.Namespace(...) in translated.ldpy. This is a genuine language-coverage result, not an oversight: 'NS = Namespace(expr)' where expr is not a literal string falls outside what '@prefix' can express.

Correction (2026-11-01, record corpus/403, defect 6): `@prefix` does take a computed IRI — `@prefix p: f<{expr}> .` transpiles (checked) — so what this note says of `@prefix` is not true; the classification is to be revisited when the region is translated again.
